$comment: Copy this to the root of the repository you want to gate, as slop.config.json.
include/exclude are globs relative to that root. Exclude test files: they are
not the code whose quality you are ratcheting, and including them lets a large
well-factored test suite mask erosion in the source.
maxDelta is the PRIMARY gate: how much one change may move each metric. Run
with `--base <the PR's base ref>` and it compares the merge base against the
head. The defaults are the paper's median HUMAN per-commit velocity, so the
gate asks whether a change degrades the codebase faster than a person
typically would. Agent checkpoints in the paper move 5x and ~7x faster.
thresholds is an OPTIONAL absolute backstop, normally null. An absolute cap on
a whole-repo ratio is a one-time budget, not a per-change allowance: the first
few changes exhaust it and every later change then fails regardless of its own
contribution. Use it only for catastrophic drift, set far above today's value.
Never put the paper's human-panel means here: those describe Python repos.
calibratedAtRulePackVersion must match rules/VERSION. Adding slop rules can
only push verbosity up, so a stale value means the ceiling is measuring
something different from what it was set against, and the gate refuses to
compare rather than reporting a meaningless regression.
